content:
# Clear a protected-path guard failure that the next log advance answers.
#
# The guard (`ci.yml`, job "protected paths (grant cross-check)") reads a
# COMMITTED copy of the log. A grant a human tapped during a session is in the
# primary checkout's live log immediately and in a committed one only when the
# daemon's next advance is pushed or merged, so a correctly gated pull request
# can fail the guard for a reason that stops being true a few minutes later,
# with no diff to push and nothing for the author to fix. GitHub re-runs
# nothing on its own, so the stale red check would sit there until somebody
# clicked it.
#
# When an advance lands on main, this re-runs the FAILED jobs of the latest CI
# run of every open pull request whose guard job failed. It re-decides nothing:
# the guard runs again and reaches its own verdict against the new log. A run
# that is still in flight is left alone.
name: guard rerun

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '.approval/log/events.jsonl'

# The whole grant this workflow needs, and nothing beside it: re-run a workflow
# run, and read the list of open pull requests. No `contents: write`, no
# checks:write, no ability to approve, merge, or comment.
permissions:
  actions: write
  pull-requests: read

# One at a time. Two advances landing minutes apart would otherwise both try to
# re-run the same runs, and the second would race the first.
concurrency:
  group: guard-rerun
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  rerun:
    name: rerun failed protected-path guards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: rerun the guard where the log is why it failed
        # Context values reach the script as environment variables and are
        # never interpolated into shell text, for the reason ci.yml's classify
        # job states: anything carried from the event is attacker-shaped input
        # and must not become shell syntax. The token is the workflow's own
        # GITHUB_TOKEN, scoped by the permissions block above; this workflow
        # reads no other secret.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: node scripts/guard-rerun.mjs
